title: New delimitation bill gives every state 50% more seats and freezes shares to 2051
dek: The revised plan meets two of the DMK's key demands, but the Congress says it will fight the bill whatever the numbers when Parliament meets on Monday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a revised delimitation package that would raise every state's Lok Sabha seats by the same 50% and freeze each state's share of the House at its present, 1971-Census-based proportion for 25 years, until 2051, according to reports. The bill, tied to bringing in one-third reservation for women, is expected to be introduced when the Lok Sabha meets on Monday, 30 November.

The government has not released the text or issued an official statement on the decision. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said it was "extraordinary and totally unacceptable" that the bill had not been shared with MPs by 6 pm on Friday although Parliament was due to take it up on Monday, according to reports.

## What changes from April

The package defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April would have raised the House's maximum strength from 543 to as many as 850 seats and linked redrawing of constituencies to fresh population figures, which southern states feared would shift weight to the faster-growing north. The new version, according to reports, keeps the 850-seat ceiling but gives every state an equal percentage rise, so that no state's share falls, and allows delimitation to go ahead without waiting for the next Census.

Those were the central demands of the DMK, whose 22 Lok Sabha members could decide the vote. DMK president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin had said Tamil Nadu's 7.18% share of seats must not fall even if the number of constituencies rises, and that the 1971-based proportions should be frozen for another 25 years, according to reports. The NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight members, had also sought a uniform 50% increase, one report said.

For West Bengal, which has 42 Lok Sabha seats, a uniform 50% rise would mean 63 seats, with its share of the House unchanged.

## The numbers

A constitutional amendment needs two-thirds of members present and voting. In April the amendment received 298 votes against 230, short of the 352 it needed. Since then, 20 of the Trinamool Congress's 28 Lok Sabha members have joined a smaller party that backs the NDA, six of the nine Shiv Sena (UBT) members have joined the Shinde faction, and the Shiromani Akali Dal's lone MP is expected to vote with the government, according to reports.

Reports differ on how close the government now is. One puts the NDA at 319 members against a threshold of about 358 in a fully attended House; another puts the threshold at 360. Even with the DMK and NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) on board, the government would be a few votes short, these reports say, leaving the YSR Congress Party's four members and abstentions potentially decisive. Neither the DMK nor the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) has formally announced its vote, though a BJP leader said he expected DMK support.

## The Opposition's position

The Congress Parliamentary Strategy Committee met at Sonia Gandhi's residence on Thursday. Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi told the meeting the party would oppose the bill whether or not it had the numbers to stop it, saying "Our decision is clear", according to reports. He has alleged that delimitation would let the BJP "gerrymander" seats before the 2029 election.

Congress deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi said the party wanted the present size of the Lok Sabha kept, the 33% women's quota brought in within the existing strength of the House, and state representation protected for 25 years. The Congress was to consult its allies on Saturday to settle a joint Opposition strategy. The Opposition accuses the government of building a two-thirds majority through defections and mergers.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi wrote this week that the April defeat "should fill our hearts with shame" and promised that "no force" would stop justice for women. The BJP says the commission will consult all parties and that no state will lose relative strength.

## What happens next

- Monday, 30 November, 11 am: Lok Sabha meets; the bill is expected to be introduced.
- Wednesday, 2 December, 11 am: Rajya Sabha meets.
- Thursday, 3 December: sittings may end.

If passed by both Houses, the amendment would also need ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.
